title: Exact GeoServer 3.0.1 GeoWebCache security and cache lifecycle comparison

source.description: The digest-pinned official GeoServer 3.0.1 image runs as a disposable loopback peer so its embedded GeoWebCache tile, rejection, administration, and exact truncate behavior can be compared with OpenGeo's current-member authorization and durable cache controls.

artifacts.name: Existing exact GeoServer service peer report

expectedOutcomes.assertion: The exact GeoServer 3.0.1 image with embedded GeoWebCache 2.0.1 advertises the layer, default style, and matrix set, returns a cold image/png cache miss followed by exact-byte sequential and concurrent hits, and returns no image for malformed and out-of-range requests.

Anonymous GeoWebCache layer inspection and truncation are denied without changing the cached tile; authenticated administration can inspect, exactly truncate, and explicitly seed the one-layer z0 cache, with subsequent reads distinguishing on-demand regeneration from a seeded hit. Source-surface and runtime-image identities remain explicit and separate.

OpenGeo separately reauthorizes current organization membership for every private route and method in the maintained service inventory and denies a revoked member before repository, cache-object, feature, coverage, render, or dispatch work; this is deliberately distinct from the upstream peer's public tile delivery and administrator-only cache controls.
